proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) and \(\mathcal L^0=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})\). By \(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), simultaneous permutation by \(\pi_0\) makes every \(L^{0,(a)}\) unit lower triangular, so every such matrix and therefore \(\mathcal L^0\) is invertible. The revised \(\texttt{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\) says that each disturbance coordinate is centered and square-integrable; the within-view independence in that assumption is part of maintained-model membership, although the covariance argument below needs only the stated second moments. By \(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\), the covariance \(\Omega=\operatorname{Cov}_P((\varepsilon^{(a)})_{a\in M})\) obeys
\[
 \Omega[(a,i),(b,j)]={\bf 1}\{i=j\}\Gamma_i[a,b].
\]
After a simultaneous reindexing that groups entries by the coordinate \(i\), this is \(\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i)\). Each block is positive definite by \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\), whence \(\Omega\succ0\). The structural equations in \(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) give \(\mathcal L^0 X=\varepsilon\) almost surely and hence
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 = (\mathcal L^0)^{-1}\Omega(\mathcal L^0)^{-\mathsf T}\succ0,
\]
where \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\) is the covariance of the conceptually full vector \((X^{(a)}:a\in M)\), including nonedge cross-blocks. Indeed, for nonzero \(v\), invertibility gives \(v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}v=((\mathcal L^0)^{-\mathsf T}v)^{\mathsf T}\Omega((\mathcal L^0)^{-\mathsf T}v)>0\). Thus every \(\Sigma^{aa}\), every principal matrix \(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\), and every within-view Schur complement \(C_A^{aa}\) is positive definite. In particular, all inverses in \(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\), \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\), and \(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) exist, and \(C_A^{aa}[r,r]>0\) whenever \(r\in U_A\).

We next prove the path criterion. In view \(b\), orthogonal projection first on the span of \(X_A^{(b)}\) and then on the residual of \(X_r^{(b)}\) is projection on the span of \(X_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(b)}\). The normal equations uniquely characterize both projections because the relevant Gram matrices are positive definite. Consequently, for \(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\),
\[
 Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}
 =Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-
   \frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}.
\]
Taking covariance with \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\), using symmetry of \(C_A^{bb}\), and invoking \(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P\!\left(Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}\right)
 =C_A^{ab}[r,t]-C_A^{ab}[r,r]\{C_A^{bb}[r,r]\}^{-1}C_A^{bb}[r,t]
 =q^{ab}(A,r,t).                                           \tag{1}
\]
This projection identity also shows that the residual state reached after removing a set \(A\) is the state in \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\), independently of the path to \(A\).

Fix a permutation whose next label after the predecessor set \(A\) is \(r\), and write \(W=U_A\setminus\{r\}\) in the order specified by the suffix of that permutation. Sequential within-view regression of \(Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)}\) gives an invertible unit triangular residualizer \(K^{(b)}\) such that the final innovation vectors satisfy
\[
 e_W^{(b)}=K^{(b)}Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)},
 \qquad e_r^{(a)}=Z_{A,r}^{(a)}.
\]
Applying (1) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_r^{(a)},e_W^{(b)})
 =\bigl(q^{ab}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)(K^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.    \tag{2}
\]
Because \(K^{(b)}\) is invertible, the left side vanishes if and only if every displayed score vanishes. Exchanging \(a\) and \(b\) likewise gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_W^{(a)},e_r^{(b)})
 =K^{(a)}\bigl(q^{ba}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.      \tag{3}
\]
Thus the two orientations required by \(\texttt{def:removed-set-compatibility-dag}\) are necessary and sufficient for all cross-view residual entries joining \(r\) to its suffix to be zero. Induction over the successive roots, with the one-coordinate suffix as the vacuous base case, proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
 \text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E.                          \tag{4}
\]
The within-view normal equations separately imply that \(R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal: each innovation is orthogonal to the predecessor span containing every earlier innovation.

It remains to prove that the positive-definite completion clause in \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) introduces no additional restriction on maintained-model inputs. For an arbitrary permutation \(\pi\), set
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Every \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit triangular in the order \(\pi\), hence invertible, so \(S_\pi\succ0\). For each \(j\in V\), let \(H_{\pi,j}\) be the principal submatrix of \(S_\pi\) on indices \(\{(a,j):a\in M\}\). If \(u\in\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\widetilde u\) is its zero extension to all view-coordinate indices, then
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}H_{\pi,j}u=\widetilde u^{\mathsf T}S_\pi\widetilde u>0,
\]
so \(H_{\pi,j}\succ0\). On a diagonal view block or an observed edge, the corresponding block of \(S_\pi\) equals
\[
 L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}=R_\pi^{ab}.
\]
Therefore \(H_{\pi,j}\) agrees with every specified entry of \(Q_{\pi,j}\) and is a positive-definite completion. This conclusion holds for every candidate permutation and every view graph \(G\), because the unobserved blocks of \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\) are used only as an existential certificate. Combining it with (4) and \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G).                                \tag{5}
\]

Finally, suppose the equivalent conditions in (5) hold. For each \(j\), take a spectral decomposition \(H_{\pi,j}=U_jD_jU_j^{\mathsf T}\), where every diagonal entry of \(D_j\) is positive. On a product probability space take independent standard Gaussian vectors \(g_j\in\mathbb R^m\) and define
\[
 (\eta_j^{(a)}:a\in M)=U_jD_j^{1/2}g_j.
\]
These coordinate stacks are mutually independent, centered, and have covariances \(H_{\pi,j}\). Put \(\eta^{(a)}=(\eta_j^{(a)}:j\in V)\) and
\[
 \widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\eta^{(a)}.
\]
Then \(\widetilde X^{(a)}=B_\pi^{(a)}\widetilde X^{(a)}+\eta^{(a)}\), and the coefficient matrices share the order \(\pi\). For each fixed view, the coordinates of \(\eta^{(a)}\) are independent centered finite-variance Gaussians, as required by the revised \(\texttt{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\). Independence of the coordinate stacks also gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_i^{(a)},\eta_j^{(b)})=0\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}((\eta_j^{(a)})_{a\in M})=H_{\pi,j}\succ0.
\]
Thus the constructed law is a member of the revised \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\); it happens to be jointly Gaussian, but Gaussianity was not imposed on the generating law \(P\). By (4), observed cross-view residual blocks are diagonal, and the within-view blocks were already shown diagonal. Their diagonal entries agree with the appropriate \(H_{\pi,j}\), so on every diagonal block and observed edge,
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta^{(a)},\eta^{(b)})=R_\pi^{ab}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
 =(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma^{ab}
\]
for all observed blocks. Hence the independently assembled coordinate stacks give a component-aligned Gaussian completion of \(\mathcal O_G\) with coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\), completing the proof.

For \(A\subseteq V\), let \(\mathcal P_A\) be the set of live prefixes from \(\varnothing\) to \(A\). We first establish directly from \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\) the dictionary invariant
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\in\mathcal P_A\}.                       \tag{6}
\]
At \(A=\varnothing\), this is the stated initialization. Suppose (6) holds for all live subsets of cardinality \(k\). Every live prefix ending at a set \(A'\) of cardinality \(k+1\) has a final transition \(A'\setminus\{r\}\to A'\). Its parent fragment is present by the induction hypothesis, and the algorithm writes exactly \(\beta(A'\setminus\{r\},r)\) into slot \(r\); hence its fragment is inserted. Conversely, every attempted insertion extends a represented live prefix along a live edge and therefore is the fragment of a member of \(\mathcal P_{A'}\). Exact trie equality removes only equal fragments. This proves (6) by induction; for a nonlive subset both sides are empty.

Fix \(F\in H_A\), and choose a representing prefix \(\rho\) using (6). Since \(A\) is live, \(\rho\) has a suffix to \(V\), so \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\ne\varnothing\). By \(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\), this completion set depends only on \(F\), and unequal fragments at \(A\) have disjoint completion sets. By \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), every source-to-sink path belongs to \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\), so each completion set is a subset of \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\). Moreover, \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) and the placement rule in \(\texttt{def:live-fragment-completions}\) imply, for every \(T\in\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\),
\[
 T\big|_{\text{rows indexed by }A}=F.                       \tag{7}
\]
Thus every retained fragment is the row projection of at least one output tuple. Distinct fragments determine disjoint nonempty subsets of the output set, and therefore
\[
 |H_A|\le |\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)|=N_{\mathrm{out}}.        \tag{8}
\]
There are \(2^p\) subsets of \(V\), so summing (8) gives
\[
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|\le 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}.           \tag{9}
\]
A subset has at most \(p-|A|\le p\) outgoing transitions, and each retained fragment is processed once. Hence the number of attempted fragment transitions is bounded by
\[
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}(p-|A|)|H_A|
 \le p\sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|
 \le p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}},
\]
which proves all assertions.

We first verify the sink semantics, without relying on an undeclared quotient oracle. Induction on subset cardinality, exactly as in the construction of \(H_A\), gives
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\text{ is a live prefix ending at }A\}.  \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, every insertion extends a represented prefix by a live edge, while the last edge of every live prefix supplies an insertion from its represented parent; the deterministic trie identifies exactly equal integer vectors. At \(A=V\), no row is unassigned. By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), the decoded full fragment of a path \(\pi\) is precisely \(T_\pi\), and by \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\) the source-to-sink paths are exactly \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\). Therefore
\[
 \{\text{decoded members of }H_V\}
 =\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}
 =\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G).                                  \tag{11}
\]
For a fixed original row label, lexicographic sorting compares all exact-real coordinates and assigns the same integer identifier exactly to numerically equal rows. Trie insertion creates a terminal only for the first occurrence of an integer vector. Equation (11) is therefore emitted without omission and with each numerical tuple appearing exactly once.

We count the construction in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ER}}\). There are \(2^p\) subset vertices and at most \(p2^{p-1}\) subset edges. For each \(A\), put
\[
 D_A^{(a)}=\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}.
\]
Expanding the covariance in \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\) gives, for every diagonal or observed cross-view block,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_A^{ab}={}&\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,U_A]
 -D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,U_A]
 -\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\\
 &+D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{12}
\]
The inverses exist by the positive-definiteness argument in \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\). Dense elimination and multiplication compute every \(D_A^{(a)}\), every block in (12), and every immutable edge row in
\[
 O\!\left((m+|E|)p^3 2^p\right)
\]
field operations. Testing all ordered edge orientations and all pairs \(r\ne t\) adds \(O(|E|p^2 2^p)\) operations and exact comparisons; forward and backward pruning add \(O(p2^p)\). Since \(p,m\ge2\), these terms are absorbed by the displayed preprocessing bound.

For a fixed original row label \(r\), at most \(K_r\le2^{p-1}\) subset edges carry that label. A lexicographic comparison of two viewwise rows examines at most \(mp\) exact-real entries. Comparison sorting and adjacent equality interning therefore use
\[
 O\!\left(mp\sum_{r\in V}K_r\log(K_r+1)\right)
 =O(mp^3 2^p)                                               \tag{13}
\]
operations, because \(\log_2(K_r+1)=O(p)\) and there are \(p\) labels. This too is absorbed by the preprocessing term. The procedure is deterministic and uses no real-valued hash.

Each row identifier requires \(O(p)\) bits because \(K_r+1\le2^{p-1}+1\). A fragment has \(p\) identifier slots, so lookup or insertion in a deterministic binary trie costs \(O(p^2)\) bit or pointer operations. By \(\texttt{lem:projection-output-bound}\), at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\) transitions are attempted. Fragment propagation therefore costs
\[
 O(p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}).                                \tag{14}
\]
Decoding \(m\) matrices with \(p^2\) entries for each of the \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\) outputs costs \(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\). Adding the bounds gives the explicit total time
\[
 O\!\left((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}+mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}\right). \tag{15}
\]

For space, all covariance states in (12) occupy \(O((m+|E|)p^2 2^p)\) real cells, the interned rows occupy \(O(mp^2 2^p)\) real cells, and the tries occupy \(O(p^2 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}})\) bits or pointers by \(\sum_A|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\). Retaining rather than streaming the decoded output adds \(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\) cells. The true generating order \(\pi_0\) supplies a path by \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), so \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\ge1\) on the maintained class. The time and space bounds are consequently
\[
 O\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\}\right).
\]
Every propagation loop ranges over a retained fragment and a live outgoing subset edge; no loop ranges over compatible permutations. This proves the final assertion.

Assume \(B^{0,(a)}=0\) for every \(a\in M\). By \(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\), \(X^{(a)}=\varepsilon^{(a)}\). For distinct \(i,j\), \(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\) gives \(\Sigma^{aa}[i,j]=0\), while \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\) gives \(\Sigma^{aa}[j,j]=\Gamma_j[a,a]>0\). Hence every \(\Sigma^{aa}\) is positive diagonal and, for \(A\subseteq V\), \(r\notin A\),
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]=0,
 \qquad \beta^{(a)}(A,r)=0.                                \tag{16}
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every order therefore induces the same all-zero coefficient tuple; in particular this holds for every compatible order.

If \(E=\varnothing\), the conjunction of score conditions defining a subset edge in \(\texttt{def:removed-set-compatibility-dag}\) is empty. Thus \(\mathcal D_G\) is the full directed subset lattice, all its vertices are live, and its source-to-sink paths are all \(p!\) permutations. By \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), all these orders are compatible. Equation (16) then gives
\[
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{0\},\qquad N_{\mathrm{out}}=1.
\]
Starting with the unique empty fragment, every transition in \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\) writes a zero row. At a fixed subset all incoming paths therefore produce the same integer fragment, which exact trie insertion retains once. Since every subset is live, there is exactly one retained fragment in each of the \(2^p\) buckets, and hence exactly \(2^p\) retained fragments in total.

Write every rational input coordinate in lowest terms. For one principal regression solve, multiply its coefficient matrix and right-hand side by the product \(d\) of the denominators of the at most \((p+1)^2\) entries in the augmented matrix. If every input numerator and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits, then
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad \operatorname{bits}(dx)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}})     \tag{17}
\]
for every scaled entry \(dx\). Multiplication of the coefficient matrix and the right-hand side by the same nonzero scalar leaves the solution unchanged. By \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), maintained-model membership makes every principal within-view covariance matrix positive definite. Its leading principal minors in any fixed ordering of \(A\) are therefore positive, so the no-pivot fraction-free recurrence has no zero pivot.

The cited \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\) states that every integer produced by the Bareiss recurrence is a signed bordered minor of the scaled augmented matrix and every division is exact. We bound those minors. If a \(k\times k\) integer matrix \(K\) has entries of magnitude below \(2^h\), the Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|
 \le\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_k}\prod_{i=1}^k|K_{i,\sigma(i)}|
 <k!\,2^{kh}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 \le kh+\lceil\log_2(k!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p\right),            \tag{18}
\]
where (17) and \(k\le p+1\) were used. The adjugate identity for the nonsingular principal covariance matrix expresses every regression coordinate as a bordered-minor numerator divided by its determinant. Reducing this pair by its greatest common divisor and choosing a positive denominator gives a canonical determinant-ratio certificate of the bit length in (18). Two coordinates, and hence two interned rows, are equal exactly when their canonical reduced certificates agree coordinatewise.

From \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\), with \(D_A^{(a)}=\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_A^{ab}={}&\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,U_A]
 -D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,U_A]
 -\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\\
 &+D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{19}
\]
After expanding the products, one entry is a sum of at most \(1+2p+p^2\) products of input rationals and regression coordinates. The score in \(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) adds two products and division by the strictly positive rational \(C_A^{bb}[r,r]\). Using (18), a common-denominator expansion, followed by greatest-common-divisor reduction, gives the coarse uniform bound
\[
 O\!\left(p^5(L_{\mathrm{bits}}+\log p)\right)              \tag{20}
\]
bits for the numerator and denominator of every directly computed covariance-state or score entry. The exact polynomial exponent is immaterial to the claim; importantly, each state is computed from the original input through (19), so this height bound is not recursively iterated through the \(2^p\) states.

The proof of \(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\) uses a number of rational field operations and exact comparisons polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(2^p\), and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\). By (17)--(20), rational addition, multiplication, division, sign comparison, and equality comparison reduce to integer operations on polynomial-length operands. Grade-school addition, multiplication, and long division take polynomially many bit operations. Euclid's algorithm also does: after at most two remainder steps its positive second operand is less than half its earlier value, so \(h\)-bit inputs require at most \(2h+1\) remainder steps, each on operands of at most \(h\) bits. Fragment keys contain \(p\) integer identifiers of \(O(p)\) bits and introduce no rational-expression growth. Decoding and writing an output costs its emitted encoding length. Multiplying these polynomial per-operation costs by the exact-real operation counts and adding the total output-writing length proves the asserted polynomial bit time. Multiplying the same height bounds by the stored covariance, row, and trie-entry counts proves polynomial bit storage. Thus no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth is forced in the stated rational maintained-model regime.

proposed.condition: Under \(P\), for every \(a\in M\), the disturbance vector \(\varepsilon^{(a)}\) has a product probability law whose coordinate marginals are centered and have finite second moments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The input law need not be Gaussian. The proof uses centered finite second moments to form covariances and the ordinary within-view LiMVAM disturbance independence for class membership; positive-definite coordinate completions are realized by newly constructed Gaussian stacks only after compatibility has been proved.

Theorem 1 establishes AMO enumeration, Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration, Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs, and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization.

Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives a framework that enumerates equivalence classes represented by local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph with polynomial delay.
Theorem 7 gives an output-dependent delay bound after linear preprocessing for projected star-query enumeration by heavy-light partitioning and interleaving.
Reverse search enumerates a connected family from a locally computable parent map without retaining a global visited set.
Fraction-free Gaussian elimination uses exact divisibility from Sylvester's identity to prevent the exponential intermediate growth of naive fraction-producing elimination.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize comparator positioning with the non-Gaussian maintained input class and with the now-proved rational bit-complexity result.

prose_updates.tldr: Many common orders can encode the same coefficient tuple in the restrictive component-aligned LiMVAM class, so traversing every compatible order can be factorial even when the causal output is a singleton. The maintained generating law may be non-Gaussian: it has the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view disturbance independence, together with component-aligned cross-view second moments and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. The population algorithm labels each removed-set transition by the immutable original-label regression row \(\beta(A,r)=\Sigma[r,A]\Sigma[A,A]^{-1}\), prunes dead subset states, interns exact rows, and merges equal live fragments. Arbitrary-view-graph path exactness follows from the generating full covariance; Gaussian coordinate stacks are introduced only to realize an existential compatible completion. The live-fragment congruence and projection charge then enumerate \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) exactly once in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space, with polynomial bit complexity for rational inputs.

project_justification.fill: Exact row interning and deterministic integer tries implement the fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. The projection lemma bounds every subset bucket by \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\). On any maintained input, the generating full covariance supplies positive-definite coordinate completions for every candidate order; after the observable path test succeeds, independently assembled Gaussian coordinate stacks realize a compatible completion. This witness construction does not impose Gaussianity on the generating law.

sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The maintained population has the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view LiMVAM disturbance independence, a shared order, component-aligned cross-view second moments, and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. The generating law need not be Gaussian. Unrestricted LiMVAM laws without component alignment, selection, transport, and arbitrary off-model covariance arrays are excluded.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, supplies the shared-order recursive-residual model and orderwise coefficient regressions under ordinary centered finite-second-moment LiMVAM disturbance independence; it does not enumerate the numerical equivalence class left by partial pairing. The present maintained class retains that non-Gaussian input scope while adding the component-aligned cross-view second-moment restriction and strict coordinate covariance positivity. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, Theorems 2--3, motivates quotienting structural representatives by the causal output, but its recursive signatures are graphical total-effect functionals rather than covariance-dependent coefficient rows. WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 1, establishes AMO enumeration; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. Those graph-distinct output counts can remain factorial when many orders share one numerical tuple. WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives the nearest general quotient framework, but its proof relies on local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph; the present right congruence is instead derived from immutable numerical row projections and live-prefix pruning. DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing, demonstrating that projection changes enumeration complexity without treating causal coefficient fibers. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the completion boundary for chordal sparsity patterns; the model-specific theorem here instead uses the generating full covariance as a certificate for an arbitrary view graph on maintained inputs. AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch provides an alternative exact enumeration paradigm but requires a locally searchable parent relation that numerical tuple classes do not supply. Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity supplies the fraction-free minor identity used to prove polynomial certificate height for the rational implementation.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The main total-cost theorem uses an ordered exact-real model and does not imply floating-point stability. A separate theorem proves deterministic output-polynomial bit time and storage for rational maintained-model inputs, including the total emitted encoding length. The result gives a \(2^p\)-state-plus-output bound, not polynomial delay and not a polynomial-in-\(p\) algorithm. The q-only graph construction is certified only for moment collections generated by the maintained non-Gaussian-permitted component-aligned model; an arbitrary off-model nonchordal edge array may pass every local q-test while admitting no positive-semidefinite completion. Exact enumeration over a continuum-valued covariance confidence region is not claimed. The generic write-once dynamic program, row sorting, and integer tries are implementation machinery rather than independent causal contributions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The contribution is confined to exact population enumeration of the coefficient-tuple frontier for the component-aligned shared-order LiMVAM class under an arbitrary fixed pairing graph. Generating disturbances satisfy the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view independence condition; cross-view second moments are component aligned and every coordinate disturbance covariance is positive definite. The generating law may be non-Gaussian. Gaussianity is used only to construct one existential full law from the completed coordinate covariance blocks, after path compatibility has been established. The result does not cover unrestricted LiMVAM mechanisms lacking component alignment. The parent covariance-region inversion is reused only as the uncertainty layer after population identification; no new limit law, floating-point guarantee, polynomial-delay result, off-model nonchordal preprocessing guarantee, or finite enumeration of a continuum covariance-region inverse is asserted. The all-zero empty-graph reduction collapses all \(p!\) orders to one tuple, and the rational implementation has polynomial bit complexity in its stated input and output parameters.
